segments.text: Your ears can feel plugged when a plane takes off.
There's actually a tube that's meant to fix that.
But that tube is normally closed.
During takeoff and landing, cabin pressure changes fast.
If the tube can't keep up, your eardrum gets stretched tight.
Yawning or swallowing opens the tube again.
That tube is called the Eustachian tube.
So it's the pressure difference behind that plugged feeling.
